story.headline: The data come from a one-dimensional field u(x,t) that develops a front which breaks up into spatiotemporal cellular chaos, and the discovered equation is a rescaled Kuramoto–Sivashinsky equation: u_t = −0.569·u·u_x − 1.184·u_xx − 1.998·u_xxxx, combining nonlinear advection, a destabilising negative diffusion and stabilising fourth-order hyperdiffusion.

key_steps.observation: Diagnostics showed a single PDE trajectory (100 snapshots × 1024 grid points, t ∈ [0, 56.6]) whose spatial mean stays constant.
key_steps.decision: Treat the dynamics as a conservation (flux-form) law and exclude source terms (1, u, u²) from the candidate library, allowing derivatives up to 4th order.
key_steps.outcome: This narrowed the search to transport, diffusion and dispersion-type terms.

key_steps.observation: Weak-form SINDy, which avoids noisy pointwise high-order derivatives, returned three terms: u·u_x, u_xx and u_xxxx.
key_steps.decision: Check that this sparse model is stable under different settings: polynomial degree 1 vs 2, and 1500 test functions.
key_steps.outcome: Coefficients were reproduced to about 0.05% (−0.5687, −1.1838, −1.998), so the identification is robust.

key_steps.observation: The plotted field shows a front dissolving into cellular chaos, the hallmark of the Kuramoto–Sivashinsky equation.
key_steps.decision: Compare the discovered model with a near-identical variant using cross-validated derivative error.
key_steps.outcome: The two variants were statistically indistinguishable. The 3-term weak-SINDy model was preferred and submitted.

key_steps.observation: A nonlinear skeleton refit (fit_skeleton) converged to coefficients 20–3000× smaller, yet reported the same valid time (6.29).
key_steps.decision: Disregard the skeleton refit and keep the weak-form coefficients.
key_steps.outcome: Bootstrap analysis later confirmed the weak-form values with tight 90% CIs (relative uncertainty ≈0.2%).

key_steps.observation: Removing any term raises BIC by more than 1100. Adding any single extra term (u_xxx, u²u_x, u_x, u²u_xxx) raises BIC by about 3.5–4.6 and reduces error by less than 1%.
key_steps.outcome: The structure is well determined, rated high confidence.

story.physical_interpretation: The −u·u_x term is Burgers-type nonlinear self-advection, which transfers energy between scales and steepens gradients. The −u_xx term is negative (anti-)diffusion that amplifies long-wavelength perturbations. The −u_xxxx term is hyperdiffusion that damps short wavelengths. Their balance selects a preferred cell size: the fastest-growing wavenumber is k* = √(1.184/(2·1.998)) ≈ 0.54, with marginal wavenumber √(1.184/1.998) ≈ 0.77. Together the three terms produce the chaotic cellular pattern typical of flame fronts, thin falling films or phase turbulence; the coefficients are simply a rescaling of the canonical KS form.
caveats: All results come from a single trajectory. The coefficients are precise for this run, but generalisation to other initial conditions or amplitudes has not been tested.
Source terms (1, u, u²) were excluded a priori on the basis of mean conservation and were never re-tested as candidates in the missing-term analysis.

Rollout metrics conflict. The tool-reported valid time is only ≈6.3 time units (about 11% of the span), while the assessment reports held-out agreement for the full horizon. For a chaotic system, pointwise trajectory divergence is expected and is not by itself evidence of model error.

The skeleton refit returned wildly different coefficients with the same valid-time score. This suggests the valid-time metric is insensitive or the optimiser failed, so valid time should not be used to rank coefficient sets here.
Domain length and boundary conditions (presumably periodic) are not documented in the data card. Grid units for x and t are also unstated.
story.recommendation: Use the model: it is a well-determined rescaled Kuramoto–Sivashinsky equation with tight coefficient uncertainties. To confirm it beyond this single run, collect one independent trajectory starting from a single Fourier mode k=6 (wavelength L/6) at data amplitude. This is predicted to sharpen the u_xx and u_xxxx coefficients most (information gain ≈33× and ≈10× over existing data) by directly probing the linear growth/decay balance.
